title: What's your preferred way to handle environment secrets in local dev?
body: I've tried `.env`, direnv, 1Password CLI, and just exporting things in my shell config. Curious what everyone lands on for a daily driver — especially when juggling five projects at once.

title: Unpopular opinion: most code reviews are performative theatre
body: I keep seeing teams where reviewers rubber-stamp huge diffs, then bikeshed variable names on a 5-line PR. Is this really the best we can do, or am I missing something?

title: When do you actually reach for a monorepo?
body: Debating whether to merge three repos at work. What's the actual threshold — team size, shared types, deploy cadence? Or is it more about org structure than tech?

title: How do you stay productive during the 3pm slump?
body: Coffee stopped working. Naps are great but not always possible. Looking for realistic habits that don't involve "just take a walk" every time.

title: Is Rust's learning curve really as bad as people say?
body: I'm comfortable with Go and TypeScript. Every time I try Rust the borrow checker humbles me in the first hour. Does it get better, or do you just build a mental model and stop fighting it?

title: Conference talks: slides or live coding?
body: I'm submitting a talk for the first time. Half the advice I read says 'never live-code', the other half says 'slides are boring'. Which actually works in practice?

title: Is it worth learning a second database engine, or should you go deep on one?
body: I've been Postgres-only for eight years. Every time I think about picking up MongoDB or ClickHouse, I wonder if I'm better off deepening my Postgres game instead. Curious how other DBAs and backend devs think about this trade-off — is breadth actually worth it, or is depth the better long game?

title: Do you write tests for personal projects, or only for work code?
body: I'm religious about tests at work — coverage gates, mutation testing, the whole thing. But the moment I open a side project on a Saturday, I just ship and pray. I can't tell if that's a healthy boundary or a bad habit I'm rationalising. Do you test your personal projects, or do you treat them as a playground where you can move fast?

title: Is 'microservices' just the default answer to every scaling question now?
body: Every time someone asks 'how do I scale X?' on any forum, the top answer is inevitably some flavour of 'split it into microservices'. But most teams I've seen who did that ended up with a distributed monolith and a much harder debugging story. When does the microservices answer actually apply, and when is it just cargo-cult advice? Genuinely curious — I've been on both sides of this and I'm not sure I have a clean heuristic yet.
